answer: Creating a new identity requires locking fresh stake through a single inlet, a rate-limited admission queue, so mass registration becomes costly and slow. Each agent must stake collateral at a registered grove, a bonded identity registry, before voting or earning. Identities traced to one island of control, meaning shared funding or infrastructure, share one vote weight. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital per fake identity and still gains no extra influence, making the attack economically irrational. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
